aims.citation: Guy W. ECDEU Assessment Manual for Psychopharmacology, Revised. Rockville, MD: US Department of Health, Education, and Welfare (DHEW Publication No. ADM 76-338); 1976. AIMS pp. 534-537 (UNVERIFIED page numbers; publisher/number/year confirmed from Maryland DoH copy).
aims.instructions: Complete the examination procedure before making ratings. Rate highest severity observed. Rate movements that occur upon activation one less than those observed spontaneously. Circle movement as well as code number that applies. Rating code: 0 = None, 1 = Minimal (may be extreme normal), 2 = Mild, 3 = Moderate, 4 = Severe.
procedure: Ask the patient whether there is anything in his/her mouth (e.g., gum, candy) and, if so, to remove it.
Ask patient about the current condition of his/her teeth. Does he/she wear dentures? Do teeth or dentures bother the patient now?
Ask whether the patient notices any movements in mouth, face, hands, or feet. If yes, ask to describe and to what extent they currently bother the patient or interfere with activities.
Have patient sit in chair with hands on knees, legs slightly apart, and feet flat on floor. Look at the entire body for movements while in this position.
Ask patient to sit with hands hanging unsupported (if male, between legs; if female wearing a dress, hanging over knees). Observe hands and other body areas.
Ask patient to open mouth. Observe tongue at rest within mouth. Do this twice.
Ask patient to protrude tongue. Observe abnormalities of tongue movement. Do this twice.
Ask patient to tap thumb, with each finger, as rapidly as possible for 10 to 15 seconds; separately with right hand, then with left hand. Observe facial and leg movements.
Flex and extend patient's left and right arms (one at a time).
Ask patient to stand up. Observe in profile. Observe all body areas again, hips included.
Ask patient to extend both arms outstretched in front with palms down. Observe trunk, legs, and mouth.
Have patient walk a few paces, turn, and walk back to chair. Observe hands and gait. Do this twice.
aims.procedureNote: Steps are wording from the Maryland DoH copy via WebFetch summariser: step text in the first clause is quoted, parenthetical/trailing elaborations are reconstructed from the standard Guy 1976 text and are UNVERIFIED verbatim. Also: 'Use a hard, firm chair without arms'; observe patient unobtrusively at rest before/after exam.

items.label: 1. Muscles of facial expression (e.g., movements of forehead, eyebrows, periorbital area, cheeks, including frowning, blinking, smiling, grimacing)
2. Lips and perioral area (e.g., puckering, pouting, smacking)
3. Jaw (e.g., biting, clenching, chewing, mouth opening, lateral movement)
4. Tongue (rate only increases in movement both in and out of mouth, NOT inability to sustain movement)

5. Upper (arms, wrists, hands, fingers): include choreic movements (rapid, objectively purposeless, irregular, spontaneous) and athetoid movements (slow, irregular, complex, serpentine). Do NOT include tremor (repetitive, regular, rhythmic)
6. Lower (legs, knees, ankles, toes) (e.g., lateral knee movement, foot tapping, heel dropping, foot squirming, inversion and eversion of foot)
7. Neck, shoulders, hips (e.g., rocking, twisting, squirming, pelvic gyrations; include diaphragmatic movements)

globalItems.label: 8. Severity of abnormal movements overall
globalItems.note: Anchors on the fetched forms say only 0-4 (None to Severe); the 'Minimal may be extreme normal' wording for 8-9 was stated by the Neurocrine booklet only.

globalItems.label: 10. Patient's awareness of abnormal movements (rate only patient's report)

dentalItems.label: 11. Current problems with teeth and/or dentures

aims.dentalNote: Upstate's copy of the form also lists 'Edentia?' and 'Do movements disappear in sleep?' (Yes/No) as items 13 and 14; Maryland copy lists only item 11 as dental. Original Guy form numbering UNVERIFIED.

scoring.total: Sum of items 1-7 (0-28). Items 8-10 are global judgements and are NOT added to the total; items 11-12 are dental status (Yes/No) and are not scored. (Neurocrine booklet: 'The sum of items 1-7 is the AIMS dyskinesia total score' and the scale 'is not linear'.) The Guy form itself prints no cut-offs for the total; the note that items 8-10 are not added is from the Neurocrine booklet, not from NIMH text - UNVERIFIED in primary form.

schoolerKane.text: Schooler-Kane research criteria (as stated by psychiatrist.com): >=3 months cumulative neuroleptic exposure; absence of other conditions that might cause involuntary movements; and either moderate dyskinetic movements (AIMS >=3) in one body area, or mild dyskinetic movements (AIMS >=2) in 2 body areas. Source says '2 body areas' (not 'two or more'), and does not use the word 'probable'. Source also states AIMS 'cannot be used by itself to diagnose TD'.
schoolerKane.citation: Schooler NR, Kane JM. Research diagnoses for tardive dyskinesia. Arch Gen Psychiatry. 1982;39(4):486-487. doi:10.1001/archpsyc.1982.04290040080014 (as listed on psychiatrist.com; original paper NOT fetched, UNVERIFIED against PubMed/JAMA)

ciwa.citation: Sullivan JT, Sykora K, Schneiderman J, Naranjo CA, Sellers EM. Assessment of alcohol withdrawal: the revised Clinical Institute Withdrawal Assessment for Alcohol scale (CIWA-Ar). Br J Addict. 1989;84(11):1353-1357. doi:10.1111/j.1360-0443.1989.tb00737.x. PMID 2597811 (Europe PMC record).
ciwa.instructions: For each item, ask the prompts and/or observe behaviour. Items 1-9 are scored 0-7 (items 'intermediate' points 2-3 and 5-6 sit between the anchors where only 0, 1, 4, 7 are described); item 10 is scored 0-4. Pulse/heart rate (beats per minute), blood pressure and time (24-hour clock) are recorded on the form but are NOT scored. Total is the sum of the 10 items.
ciwa.itemOrderNote: Item order matches the form from the standard form layout; NOT confirmed from a fetched page; the ADAI summary lists items in a different order (nausea, tactile, tremor, auditory, sweats, visual, anxiety, headache, agitation, orientation). Order is not scored. Anchors 2-3 and 5-6 labelled '(intermediate)' per source. Anchors for tactile/auditory/visual 1-3 reconstructed from ADAI summary: UNVERIFIED verbatim.

items.label: 1. Nausea and vomiting (ask 'Do you feel sick to your stomach? Have you vomited?')
options: Constant nausea, frequent dry heaves and vomiting

items.label: 2. Tremor (arms extended and fingers spread apart)
options: Not visible, but can be felt fingertip to fingertip
Severe, even with arms not extended

items.label: 3. Paroxysmal sweats
options: Beads of sweat obvious on forehead

items.label: 4. Anxiety (ask 'Do you feel nervous?')
options: Moderately anxious, or guarded, so anxiety is inferred
Equivalent to acute panic states as seen in severe delirium or acute schizophrenic reactions

items.label: 5. Agitation
options: Paces back and forth during most of the interview, or constantly thrashes about

items.label: 6. Tactile disturbances (itching, pins-and-needles sensations, burning, numbness, feeling of bugs crawling on or under the skin)
options: Very mild itching, pins and needles, burning or numbness
Mild itching, pins and needles, burning or numbness
Moderate itching, pins and needles, burning or numbness

items.label: 7. Auditory disturbances (ask 'Are you more aware of sounds around you? Are they harsh? Do they frighten you? Are you hearing anything that is disturbing to you? Are you hearing things you know are not there?')
options: Very mild harshness or ability to frighten
Mild harshness or ability to frighten
Moderate harshness or ability to frighten

items.label: 8. Visual disturbances (ask 'Does the light appear to be too bright? Is its color different? Does it hurt your eyes? Are you seeing anything that is disturbing to you? Are you seeing things you know are not there?')
9. Headache, fullness in head (ask 'Does your head feel different? Does it feel like there is a band around your head?' Do not rate for dizziness or lightheadedness)
10. Orientation and clouding of sensorium (ask 'What day is this? Where are you? Who am I?')
options: Oriented and can do serial additions
Cannot do serial additions or is uncertain about date
Disoriented for date by no more than 2 calendar days
Disoriented for date by more than 2 calendar days

scoring.note: Maximum 67 (stated on the form); equals 9 items x 7 + orientation 4.

thresholds.text: Patients scoring less than 10 do not usually need additional medication for withdrawal. The maximum score is 67 (see instrument).

thresholds.source: West Virginia University Medicine NCCU alcohol detoxification protocol/form
thresholds.text: Scores of 8 to 15 indicate moderate withdrawal (marked autonomic arousal); and scores of 15 or more indicate severe withdrawal. Protocol: CIWA >0 but <8 and stable vitals: no medication; >8 but <15: lorazepam 2 mg PO/IM; >=15 (>15 in text) or DBP >110: lorazepam 2 mg q1h until CIWA <15. Call MD if >6 mg lorazepam in 3 h.
thresholds.caveat: Protocol uses strict < and > so exact 8 and 15 are unassigned; the same form states <10 does not usually need medication. 'Mild' (<8) is implied by the protocol, not worded as 'mild' in the fetched summary.

scoring.suggestedBands: Mild/minimal: <8 (WVU protocol, no medication) or <10 (form footnote); Moderate: 8-15; Severe: >=15. Sources conflict; show both.

sources: Europe PMC REST record for PMID 2597811
ciwa.caveat: Item prompt wording in parentheses and item order were NOT confirmed verbatim from a fetched page (summariser could not quote at length); anchors were fetched from the ADAI copy in paraphrase.

cows.citation: Wesson DR, Ling W. The Clinical Opiate Withdrawal Scale (COWS). J Psychoactive Drugs. 2003;35(2):253-259. doi:10.1080/02791072.2003.10400007. PMID 12924748 (Europe PMC record).
cows.instructions: For each item, write in the number that best describes the patient's signs or symptom. Rate on just the apparent relationship to opiate withdrawal. For example, if heart rate is increased because the patient was jogging just prior to assessment, the increased pulse rate would not add to the score. (Instruction paraphrase from the NIDA summary; verbatim wording UNVERIFIED.) Total score is the sum of all 11 items.

items.label: 1. Resting pulse rate (beats/minute; measured after patient is sitting or lying for one minute)
2. GI upset (over last 1/2 hour)
options: Multiple episodes of diarrhea or vomiting

items.label: 3. Sweating (over past 1/2 hour not accounted for by room temperature or patient activity)
options: No report of chills or flushing
Subjective report of chills or flushing
Flushed or observable moistness on face
Beads of sweat on brow or face

items.label: 4. Tremor (observation of outstretched hands)
options: Tremor can be felt, but not observed

items.label: 5. Restlessness (observation during assessment)
options: Reports difficulty sitting still, but is able to do so
Frequent shifting or extraneous movements of legs/arms
Unable to sit still for more than a few seconds

items.label: 6. Yawning (observation during assessment)
options: Yawning once or twice during assessment
Yawning three or more times during assessment

items.label: 7. Pupil size
options: Pupils pinned or normal size for room light
Pupils possibly larger than normal for room light
Pupils so dilated that only the rim of the iris is visible

items.label: 8. Anxiety or irritability
options: Patient reports increasing irritability or anxiousness
Patient so irritable or anxious that participation in the assessment is difficult

items.label: 9. Bone or joint aches (if patient was having pain previously, only the additional component attributed to opiates withdrawal is scored)
options: Patient reports severe diffuse aching of joints/muscles
Patient is rubbing joints or muscles and is unable to sit still because of discomfort

items.label: 10. Gooseflesh skin
options: Piloerection of skin can be felt or hairs standing up on arms

items.label: 11. Runny nose or tearing (not accounted for by cold symptoms or allergies)
options: Nasal stuffiness or unusually moist eyes
Nose constantly running or tears streaming down cheeks

scoring.rangeNote: Max 48 computed from item maxima (4+5+4+4+5+4+5+4+4+5+4); not printed on the fetched source - UNVERIFIED as a stated figure.

bandSource.text: Score: 5- 12 = mild; 13-24 = moderate; 25-36 = moderately severe; more than 36 = severe withdrawal

buprenorphine.source: UNM Emergency Medicine buprenorphine induction guide
buprenorphine.text: 'If your patient has a COWS score >8' discuss buprenorphine and start induction in the ED if no contraindications; contraindications section says 'COWS >= 8'; COWS 4-7: do not give buprenorphine in ED, consider home induction. Internal inconsistency (>8 vs >=8) in the document.
buprenorphine.caveat: Single institutional protocol; broad guideline sources (SAMHSA TIP 63, ASAM) not fetched. Other widely cited thresholds (e.g., COWS >=12) UNVERIFIED.
